name: First light
say: Half past five and flat calm: two knots of air, a grey glassy channel and the island a shape on the horizon. The best hour of the day to run across, and the fish are feeding

name: Morning
say: Eight o'clock. A light southerly, 7 to 10 knots in the channel and less under the island. Easy going in any direction

name: Midday
say: Noon, 7 or 8 knots from the south and the haze burning off. The westerly has not arrived yet

name: Afternoon westerly
say: Four o'clock and the sea breeze is in: 13 knots from the south-west at Queens Gate, 10 from the west in the channel, with a short chop on it. Avalon stays calm in the island's lee

name: Evening
say: Half past seven. The westerly is easing to 8 or 9 knots and the light is going gold. The evening bite, and a following sea home to Long Beach

name: Sunday at dawn
say: Sunday, half past five. Five knots from the south-east and a whole day ahead
